root_idea.summary: The supplied lexical evidence centers on disorderly or corrupt action, with related nominal imagery of dry, matted hair and straggling vegetation.
root_idea.development: The evidence links corrupting or mischievous action with states of untended, matted, or straggling growth. No matched Maqāyīs or Mufradāt entry was supplied, so no stronger root-level historical development is asserted.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Classical Arabic Form I citation form عَثَا rather than the inflected QAC lemma candidate.

senses.definition: To act corruptly or do mischief.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrences, the active imperfect appears in admonitory constructions, commonly with فِي الْأَرْضِ (“in the land” or “on the earth”); the usage may carry an emphatic force, “to the utmost degree.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To act wrongfully, injuriously, or unjustly, including uses where corruption is not specifically implied.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical Arabic use of the Form I verb, distinct from the Quranic framing of corrupt or mischievous action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of hair: to become dry and matted after being left uncombed for a long time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage said of the hair of the head.
Recorded as the primary nominal signification of this headword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Straggling plants or herbage; by extension, the earth’s plants or herbage when they have dried up or become yellow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metaphorical application to vegetation, including the expression شَابَ عُثَى الأَرْضِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A long lock or mass of hair hanging below the ear or reaching the shoulder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal hair term with variant plural vocalizations recorded in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The state of hair when it has become dry and matted and has been left uncombed for a long time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal description of an unkempt condition of the hair of the head.
An adjective applied to a person or specifically to a thick beard.
The related feminine عَثْوَاءُ denotes a female hyena, while the recorded plural forms عُثْوٌ and عُثْىٌ denote a group of hyenas.
An appellation applied to an old woman, distinct from the related zoological use for a female hyena.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thick, gross, or coarse in size.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of bodily or material bulk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Foolish or stupid; heavy or dull.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of mental dullness or heaviness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One whose color inclines to blackness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of a person or other individual whose coloring is blackish.
This color sense is reported with an alternative association to abundant hair.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers the Quran-attested corrupting/mischief sense and the broader wrongful-action use.
Specialized usage said of dry, matted hair.
Metaphorical vegetation and dried or yellowed herbage use.
Long lock or mass of hair.
Pointer-only cross-reference with no independent definition.
Explicitly points back to the same corrupting-action sense represented by the Quranic verb.
Hyena terminology, including feminine and plural forms.
An individual whose coloring inclines to blackness.
A blackish color, with an alternatively reported association with abundant hair.
